name: Dialog
summary: Presents modal content with focus management and dismissal.

useWhen: Blocking a task until a decision is made
Working through a step that holds the page, such as reviewing changes or editing a few fields
avoidWhen: Confirming an action that cannot be undone; use AlertDialog

obligations: Expose dialog semantics and modal behavior by making sibling content inert.
Trap focus while open and restore focus when closed.
Support Escape and backdrop dismissal when enabled.
Offer a way to dismiss a sheet without dragging: Escape, an outside press, and a labelled close button.

behavior: A Dialog renders in a portal and makes the content outside it inert while it is open.
Page scrolling is locked while a Dialog is open.
When overlays are stacked, Escape closes the topmost one.
Closing returns focus to the element that was focused when the Dialog opened.
If the element that opened the Dialog has left the DOM when the Dialog closes or unmounts, focus moves to the nearest ancestor recorded at opening that is still connected and focusable.
That move happens only when focus would otherwise be on the document body, and with no such ancestor focus stays there.
trigger is optional and renders the element that opens the Dialog.
Open state is controlled with open and onOpenChange, or starts from defaultOpen when uncontrolled.
Optional description and actions render with the stable muxui-dialog__description and muxui-dialog__actions selectors.
Mux UI part classes stay when consumer backdrop, panel, title, description, content, actions, and close classes are applied.
Default styling is preserved unless the consumer overrides it.
With dismissable set to false, Escape, an outside press, and the trigger do not close the Dialog.
A Dialog with dismissable set to false has no built-in close button.
A button with slot="close" in the content or actions still closes it.
Pressing a close-slot button closes an uncontrolled Dialog and calls onOpenChange(false).
A controlled Dialog stays open until its owner sets open to false.
presentation sets where the Dialog appears: center, the default, in the middle of the viewport, or sheet along the bottom edge of the visible viewport.
A sheet slides up from below the viewport and leaves the same way without fading, while its backdrop fades its scrim colour.
A drag on a sheet starts on its grip, title, or description; the content, the actions, the close button, and any control inside the title or description keep their own presses.
A drag moves the sheet down with the pointer and never above its resting place.

Releasing a drag lower than the smaller of 96 pixels and half the sheet's height, or flinging it down at 800 pixels a second or faster after at least 16 pixels, dismisses the sheet as Escape does; any other release returns it to rest.
A drag dismissal calls onOpenChange(false) as Escape does, so a controlled owner that keeps the Dialog open keeps the sheet open, and the sheet returns to rest.
Pressing a sheet's grip, title, or description moves neither focus nor the selection of a focused field.
A sheet's content scrolls on its own and the panel does not, so the grip, title, and close button stay in view.
A sheet fits the visible viewport, so it rises above an on-screen keyboard, and it pads its edges by the safe-area insets.
A sheet that is not dismissable has no grip and cannot be dragged.
Under reduced motion a sheet appears and leaves at once, shows no grip, and cannot be dragged.
The sheet's panel carries data-muxui-state-dragging while a drag holds it.
accessibility: Require a title, aria-label, or aria-labelledby and expose role dialog with modal focus containment and outside-content exclusion.
Generate an accessible title relationship when title is provided.
Provide a labelled close button when dismissable.
Associate description through a stable generated ID and merge it with caller aria-describedby references.
Hide a sheet's grip from assistive technology, since a drag only repeats Escape, an outside press, and the labelled close button.
